# CS 27.927 — Additional tests

> [!summary]
> CS 27.927 sets the additional tests for the rotor drive system of a small
> rotorcraft. It is a CS-27 specification, not a CS-E one, and the rotorcraft
> applicant owns it. Two regimes apply: dynamic and endurance testing, and
> torque application tests where the pilot does not control engine output
> directly. A single sentence covers loss of oil pressure. The paragraph is much
> shorter than its CS-29 counterpart, and the difference is substantive.

## Requirement

The verbs below are CS-27's own. They bind the rotorcraft applicant, not the
engine applicant. See `## Bearing on this engine` for what reaches CS-E.

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **(a)** | Perform any additional dynamic, endurance and operational tests, and vibratory investigations, needed to determine that the rotor drive mechanism is safe. | Required |
| **(b)** | Make the test below if turbine engine torque output to the transmission can exceed the highest engine or transmission torque rating limit, and that output is not directly controlled by the pilot under normal operating conditions. | Required |
| **(b)(1)** | With all engines operating, make 200 applications of torque, each of 10 seconds, at a torque at least equal to the lesser of the two values in (b)(1)(i) and (b)(1)(ii). | Required |
| **(b)(1)(i)** | The first candidate value is the maximum torque used in meeting CS 27.923 plus 10%. | Statement |
| **(b)(1)(ii)** | The second candidate value is the maximum attainable torque output of the engines, assuming that torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. | Statement |
| **(b)(2)** | For a multi-engine rotorcraft, with each engine in turn becoming inoperative, apply to the remaining transmission torque inputs the maximum torque attainable under probable operating conditions, assuming that torque limiting devices, if any, function properly. Test each transmission input at that maximum torque for at least 15 minutes. | Required |
| **(b)(3)** | Conduct the tests of this paragraph on the rotorcraft, at the maximum rotational speed intended for the power condition of the test, and absorb the torque by the rotors to be installed. | Required |
| **(b)(3)** | Other ground or flight test facilities with other appropriate methods of torque absorption may be used, if the conditions of support and vibration closely simulate those of a test on the rotorcraft. | Permitted |
| **(c)** | Show by tests that the rotor drive system can operate under autorotative conditions for 15 minutes after the loss of pressure in the rotor drive primary oil system. | Required |

Sub-point (b)(1)(ii) is worded more broadly than its CS-29 equivalent. CS-27
asks for "The maximum attainable torque output of the engines, assuming that
torque limiting devices, if any, function properly" [ext CS 27.927(b)(1)(ii)].
CS-29 narrows the same value to what is attainable "under probable operating
conditions" [ext CS 29.927(b)(1)(ii)]. The OEI case in (b)(2) carries the
narrower wording in both codes.

Sub-point (c) is one sentence: "It must be shown by tests that the rotor drive
system is capable of operating under autorotative conditions for 15 minutes
after the loss of pressure in the rotor drive primary oil system"
[ext CS 27.927(c)]. There is no Category A and Category B split, no 30-minute
case, and no prescribed load schedule. [[CS 29.927|CS 29.927(c)]] sets all
three.

CS-27 has no overspeed test. The 50 overspeed runs of [ext CS 29.927(d)] have no
counterpart here, and neither does the "without intervening disassembly"
condition of [ext CS 29.927(f)].

### Acceptable means — AMC1 27.927, variable rotor speed

| Ref | Obligation | Strength |
|---|---|---|
| **AMC1 27.927(a)** | This AMC supplements FAA AC 27-1B, § AC 27.927, and should be used in conjunction with that AC when demonstrating compliance with CS 27.927. | Accepted method |
| **AMC1 27.927(b)(1)** | A variable rotor speed function allows running at different rotor speed levels, for lower noise or better rotorcraft performance. Beyond the endurance test of CS 27.923, additional tests may be needed to show that a rotor drive system with variable rotor speed is safe. | Statement |
| **AMC1 27.927(b)(2)** | To substantiate acceptable vibration and dynamic behaviour across the available range of rotor speeds, consider performing specific test investigations as prescribed in CS 27.927(a). | Accepted method |
| **AMC1 27.927(b)(2)** | Evaluate the need for representative test runs at the different torque and rotor speed combinations, covering steady states and transient conditions to be encountered in operation, and agree it with the Agency. | Accepted method |

The two codes carry the same variable rotor speed AMC, word for word apart from
the paragraph numbers and the FAA advisory circular each one names
[ext AMC1 27.927], [ext AMC1 29.927].

### What CS-27 does not have

The asymmetry runs the other way as well, and it is larger than the AMC above.

- **No AMC for loss of lubrication.** CS-29 carries `AMC1 29.927(c)`, a test
  procedure of some 26,000 characters: entry condition, drainage, depleted-oil
  run, simulated landing, a reduction factor, a component condition class and a
  formula. CS-27 has nothing for its sub-point (c). It is recorded in
  [[CS 29.927]].
- **No AMC or GM for point 917.** CS-27 has the specification [ext CS 27.917]
  and nothing else: a search of CS-27 Amendment 10 for an AMC or GM to point
  27.917 returns nothing. CS-29 carries three, and what they require is in
  [[CS 29.917]].
- **No AMC or GM for point 923.** The same gap applies to the endurance test:
  CS-27 has the specification [ext CS 27.923] and no published means. It is
  recorded in [[CS 27.923]].

An applicant certificating against CS-27 therefore has the one-sentence
obligation of CS 27.927(c) and no published means of complying with it.

## Bearing on this engine

CS 27.927 creates no CS-E obligation. The tests are run on the rotor drive
system, which is not part of the engine type design. Two test conditions are
defined by engine data.

The torque application tests assume the engine's torque limiting devices work,
in (b)(1)(ii) and again in (b)(2). Where that limiter is the EECS, its integrity
is engine-side evidence under [[CS-E 50]], and its failure behaviour reaches the
safety analysis of [[CS-E 510]]. The torque the engines can deliver follows from
the ratings declared under [[CS-E 40]] and must reach the installer through the
installation instructions required by [[CS-E 20]].

The OEI case in (b)(2) runs for at least 15 minutes with one engine inoperative,
exactly as in CS-29. The same open item applies to both codes, and is recorded
in [[CS 29.927]].

CS-27 asks the engine for less than CS-29 does. It needs no rotational speed
expected from an engine control device failure, because it has no overspeed
test. An engine offered for both codes still has to supply that figure, so the
CS-29 case governs the data set.

[VERIFY: whether the installation is certificated under CS-27 or CS-29. The
paragraphs differ in substance, above all for loss of lubrication. [[CS-E 30]]
carries the same open item.]
